item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Ah, that explains it not being obvious. I'm rather green with the whole wikidot code stuff. Seems we have rather a proliferation of standards these days, between multiple flavours of HTML, CSS, Javascript, PHP-MySQL, BBCode, wikipedia markup, markdown, and now this. But it is at least largely one of the more logical and readable formats, and seems to be - through those module inclusions - extremely powerful and flexible.

Bones I'm now going to read as talking like Data from STTNG, as he tends towards a similar verbal affect ;)

I know couple can sometimes be used for more than two, but on an international standpoint it does also carry the direct meaning of a (not necessarily matched) pair, or at least an uncertain number in that region (1 to 3, or less often (1 or) 2 to 4); "(a) few" is more general on that front, though potentially even more ambiguous - "several" may work, though again which of the two is larger may depend on your locale. In my own it's couple-few-several(-many-lots) but I know it can vary. So I hope I haven't messed up your text too much with that question.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I've fixed the a/an error. "Couple" was being used in the more informal capacity of "small number"; I've changed it to few to be clearer. All of Night's dialogue is a little smaller than it'd normally be and is shrunk to 90% — one line was at 80% and has been brought in line to the rest.

Bones not speaking in contractions is intentional. It's just meant to be a minor quirk to differentiate him.

The font is alpha_echoregular and is imported onto the page by [[include component:chicago-spirit]], which is the first line in the source code (which imports it onto itself from the Chicago Spirit Theme.

item.content:encoded:
Mr Night Shamalamadingdong. What a twist! Masquerades are everywhere in this game.

presumed typos 'n' stuff -

  • "his superiors had put him up in an silly ghost costume" … perhaps edited from "an idiotic"?
  • "a couple" of cookies (implying two), one taken… twenty minutes later, they've "almost" run out?
  • one of Night's lines of text is smaller than the others and, at least on my screen, borderline unreadable due to the combination of font and point-size.
  • sure there was something else but can't remember, or see it on skimming through again

…and one of the quartet seems to talk in an odd fashion lacking natural contractions, but that may just be an affectation.

Also, what is that font and how did you get it to render? I can't see the secret source in the wikicode version, and I don't recognise it as one I have installed.

item.title: Black As Night: Part 1
item.content:encoded:
This is the new Part 1 of Black as Night, a series I'm working on about Mr. Night, the end of the Chicago Spirit and the rise of the Chicago Spectre. Part 2 and the Hub will be coming soon, but in the meantime you can skip to Part 3, which has been up for some time.

  • The tale can only have one survivor; how you define that is up to you.
  • One of the characters has to end up in a costume, against their will, to solve some issue that comes up in the tale.

The one survivor is, of course, Night. Night ends up in a ghost costume to act the part of a sycophant to Robinson/Bones/Flannagan/Schulz, in the Tommy costume to pretend to not be himself, and a Schulz costume to answer the door. He doesn't really want to be in any of those.

Big thanks to PeppersGhost for talking about Mr. Night (who is his character) on IRC over six months ago. Most of what was discussed on that didn't end up making it into this tale (to say this is drastically different from how I first imagined the Part 1 of Black as Night is a massive understatement), but there are elements that influenced the tale, as well as the later entries in this series.

Another big thanks goes to The Great Hippo, who gave me some really good crit that lead to a large rewrite of the tale, and strengthened it a lot. The feedback they gave was really good, and this would have been a lot worse without it.

And finally, thanks to Stallmantic and KindlyTurtleClem for looking at this as well.
